methodological_rigor.justification: Rigorous method development with comprehensive validation on multiple RNA targets (G4 HIV-1 LTR, hairpin loop GAAGGAAGG, 5'UTR library). Negative controls specified (non-azide VQ compounds). Statistical framework clearly defined: Fisher's exact test with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR control (q<0.01), Z-score normalization with robust statistics (median absolute deviation), and minimum read depth threshold (1000). Two independent technical replicates shown for proof-of-principle experiments.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Assay development paper addressing technical barrier in RNA-targeting drug discovery. BIVID-MaP enables screening for variant-specific drug interactions, potentially guiding therapeutic selection. However, clinical application remains prospective; no clinical validation, patient samples, or therapeutic efficacy data provided. Method is foundational tool rather than direct clinical advance.

reporting_quality.justification: Methods section extraordinarily detailed: precise chemical synthesis protocols, sequencing parameters, bioinformatics pipeline with explicit equations (Equations 1-6), quality control parameters, and reagent specifications. All four primary assays (BIVID-MaP, SHAPE-MaP, DMS-MaPseq, gel shift) reproducibility noted. Supplementary Data referenced for sequences. Missing: statement of data availability for sequencing reads, cost-benefit analysis, broader method generalizability testing beyond G4 and hairpin structures.

novelty_literature.justification: First high-throughput method to systematically identify variant-specific RNA-small molecule interactions at single-nucleotide resolution. BIVID-MaP uniquely preserves sequence information through RT deletion profiling rather than RT termination, overcoming technical limitations of prior approaches. Addresses previously unmet need in RNA-targeting drug development. Method applicable to cancer-associated mutations affecting RNA druggability.

writing_presentation.justification: Well-organized methods paper with clear principle figure (Figure 1a-b) explaining BIVID-MaP overview and deletion detection mechanism. Methods narrative follows logical experimental workflow from DNA template design through sequencing analysis. Mathematical equations precisely defined with proper notation. Some sections highly technical (reverse transcription buffer optimization, bioinformatics filtering) but appropriate for specialized molecular methods audience.

key_strengths: First systematic method enabling detection of variant-specific RNA-small molecule interactions with single-nucleotide resolution
Rigorous statistical validation with Fisher's exact test, Benjamini-Hochberg multiple testing correction (q<0.01), and Z-score normalization
Comprehensive technical documentation: explicit equations, sequencing parameters, negative controls, and quality thresholds (1000 read depth minimum)
Validation across multiple RNA structures (G4, hairpin) and large-scale 5'UTR mutation library (cancer-associated somatic mutations from COSMIC)
Clear demonstration of mutation-dependent binding changes to G4-binding ligands affecting drug selectivity
key_concerns: Limited to in vitro RNA binding assays without cellular or therapeutic validation in cancer models
Clinical translational path speculative; no demonstration that identified variant-specific interactions affect drug efficacy in patients
Method scope validation restricted to G-quadruplex and simple hairpin structures; generalizability to complex RNA tertiary structures unclear
Two technical replicates for proof-of-principle experiments; no power analysis or sample size justification provided
No open-access sequencing data statement; reproducibility dependent on reagent availability and synthesis capability
chief_reviewer.rationale: Innovative technical contribution addressing genuine methodological gap in RNA drug discovery. Rigorous development justifies tier 2, though clinical relevance requires future validation.
